boundary_observations: The peer-reviewed article explicitly says the dataset was divided because of a 10,000-record-per-file limit.
Table 1 lists 17 date or part-number ranges plus separate Combine and Processed Version aggregate views.
Table 2 has five selected APT or payload-category rows, but neither the article nor the Zenodo metadata binds those rows to five complete, disjoint executions.
The public artifacts aggregate benign and malicious records and expose no defensible whole-campaign start/end identity without inspecting sealed content.
linux_apt_dataset_2024.counting_decision: The 17 CSVs, five APT or payload categories, aggregate files, rows, dates, hosts, and sensors do not create independent cases.
linux_apt_dataset_2024.reconsideration_gate: Only an isolated curator may assign positive credit after proving a complete unique execution boundary and a unique all-required-telemetry capture without exposing labels or outcomes to model developers.

boundary_observations: The public record describes one combined physical and cyber scenario involving a robot dog, webcam, Wi-Fi network, physical intrusion, sabotage-hardware installation, and robot takeover.
The release exposes robot-unit audit logs for attack and normal conditions but does not publicly prove complete telemetry coverage of the webcam and other participating devices.
Attack and clean conditions, devices, and log records cannot expand one scenario into multiple cases.
attackmate_robotdog.required_before_case_credit: The curator must prove a complete attack execution boundary, sufficient campaign-wide coverage, unique telemetry identity, and no AttackMate-family or cross-source overlap.

ainception_storylines.publisher: The AInception Consortium, European Defence Fund project GA 101103385
boundary_observations: The official record describes SL100, SL300, and SL700 as three distinct military cyber-defence storylines with multi-step attack chains.
The record reports 15 complete simulations, but each simulation is a variant or execution of one of the three storyline definitions.
The three storyline definitions are the only current metadata-level case credits; the 15 archives cannot be counted as 15 unique chains.
The archives contain raw logs, network data, timelines, and labelled subsets and therefore remain sealed from the model-development role.
ainception_storylines.required_before_case_credit: The curator must preselect at most one complete execution per storyline, hash the retained archive, prove complete coverage, and audit overlap with AttackMate-derived and other emulation sources.

additional_screened_sources_not_counted.reason: The RAID 2025 release reports 114 instances of one game; public metadata does not prove 114 unique chain definitions, so no credit is assigned.

additional_screened_sources_not_counted.source: Measuring Attack Observability in Cloud Telemetry Logs
additional_screened_sources_not_counted.reason: The public README reports 35 subscription-level attack scripts across AWS, Azure, and GCP, but does not establish 35 complete multi-stage campaign definitions.

additional_screened_sources_not_counted.source: Cyber-Physical Power System Dataset for Cyber Security of Digital Substations
additional_screened_sources_not_counted.reason: The public record lists operating conditions and individual attack types; it does not establish distinct complete APT-style chains.
The record is anonymous and reports three attack scenarios without an authoritative chain-boundary publication; it remains excluded.
The record exposes only the paper PDF and no authoritative raw telemetry artifact.
